newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt firm but quiet on IMF, budget news.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt firm but quiet on IMF, budget news.

text.p: Russian debt prices were firmer on Monday morning following the release of IMF money and news that parliament had passed the first reading of the 1997 draft budget.

But traders said activity in Vneshekonombank paper and MinFins was very thin. "It is certainly slightly firmer, but it is perhaps not quite as strong (as it could be) because of the holiday coming up," one European bank trader said.
He said the market would wait to see if there was any more profit-taking in store before taking bigger positions.

Traders said the market is also waiting to see when the International Monetary Fund will release the November and December tranches of its $10 billion loan package. On Friday, the IMF board agreed to disburse the delayed October tranche of $336 million.
But there was relief that the first reading of the budget had got through the Duma on Sunday. The Communist Party said it had backed it in the interests of national unity.
Vnesh dollar paper was up 1/4 of a point to a bid of 77 cents in the dollar. MinFins were up to 1/2 a point higher.
